# local 0005: mcs51 --stack-auto --xstack: stack underflow assertion for calls through a pointer to a function that returns a struct

- Category: [Fixes](../../fix.md)
- Evidence: tested on r17193
- Recommended action: Apply the patch. With --xstack, programs with these calls then compile and do not link, for the reasons under Related.
- Patch: [local-0005.patch](../../patches/local-0005.patch), commit [`63bc0b13d`](https://github.com/mdmower/sdcc/commit/63bc0b13d78fa18c42c05b8834de369e74bce9f3). Applies to r17193 without the other patches.
<!-- end of generated block -->

## Finding

With `--stack-auto --xstack` the compiler stops with the internal error "stack underflow" for
calls through a pointer to a function that returns a struct. The assertion is in `emitpop` in
`src/mcs51/gen.c`, at line 313. The file below was compiled with
`sdcc -mmcs51 --stack-auto --xstack -c x1.c` on r17176. The compiler printed error 9 with that
text, exited with status 1, and did not write an output file.

```c
struct s { unsigned char a; int b; unsigned char c; };

struct s viaPointer (struct s (*fp) (void))
{
  struct s r = fp ();
  return r;
}
```

The compiler stops in the same place when the body of `viaPointer` is `return fp ();`, and with
`--model-large --stack-auto --xstack`. The file compiles with `--stack-auto` alone and with
`--xstack` alone. With `--stack-auto --xstack`, a call of such a function by its name compiles,
and so does a call through a pointer to a function that returns `int`. r17192 with the earlier
patches of this report also stops for such calls, with `--fomit-frame-pointer` added too, and with
`--xstack` alone when the calling function is `__reentrant`.

## Cause

Callers pass the address of the result object as a hidden pointer. Since
[r14382](https://sourceforge.net/p/sdcc/code/14382/), `pushbigreturn` writes that pointer to the
external stack with `movx` when `--xstack` is in effect and the result object is on the stack, and
`genCall` removes it with three `dec _spx`. `genPcall` has three calls of `emitpop (0)` for this.
Each call emits `dec sp` and decrements the counter `_G.stack.pushed`, which `pushbigreturn` does
not increment in this case. The counter becomes negative, and the assertion in `emitpop` fails. In
gdb on r17176, it fails in the first of the three calls, where `_G.stack.pushed` is -1.

## Fix

`genPcall` emits three `dec _spx` when `options.useXstack` is set and the result object is on the
stack. Otherwise it calls `emitpop (0)` three times, as before. When the result object is not on
the stack, `pushbigreturn` pushes the pointer on the internal stack with `--xstack` too.

## Verification

`support/regression/tests/funptr-struct-return-xstack.c` has 12 assertions. Of the regression
variants, only `mcs51-xstack-auto` passes `--stack-auto --xstack`. A default build does not build
its library, so it was built with `make -C device/lib model-mcs51-small-xstack-auto`. On that
variant, the compiler of r17192 with the earlier patches of this report stops with "stack
underflow" for the new test, for `funptrsstructreturn`, and for `bug-3847`. With the patch the
three compile, and the link fails with "Undefined Global spx", which is the first fault under
Related. With the patch and a change of five lines to `genRet` and `genFunction` that is not in
the patch, the new test passes with 12 of 12 assertions on that variant, `funptrsstructreturn`
with 16 of 16, and `bug-3847` with 22 of 22. One function of the new test makes 100 calls, which
overflow a stack when each call leaves the hidden pointer on it.

On host, the six mcs51 variants (the four models, and small and large with `--stack-auto`), stm8,
and ucz80, the new test passes with and without the source change, because these variants do not
pass `--xstack`.

Nine files with such calls were compiled with eight sets of options, with and without the patch.
47 of the 72 compilations succeed without the patch, and their assembly is identical with it. 17
stop with "stack underflow" without the patch and succeed with it. In their assembly, a call
through a pointer has three `movx` writes before `lcall sdcc_call_dptr` and three `dec _spx` after
it, as a call by name has. The other 8 are of the file with a call through a literal address,
which Related describes.

For mcs51-large-stack-auto, the assembly of the other regression tests is identical with and
without the patch. With the series of this report up to the patch for #3992 applied to r17192,
the regression suite has 0 failures for host, the six mcs51 variants, stm8, and ucz80. The
diagnostics suite has 0 failures for mcs51, mcs51-large, mcs51-stack-auto, z80, and stm8.

## Related

- With `--xstack`, the code of functions that return a struct has faults of its own, and calls by
  name have them too. On `mcs51-xstack-auto` with r17192 and the earlier patches of this report,
  `structreturn`, `bug-3849`, and `bug-4157` do not link because of `spx`, and `bug-4158` links and
  fails 10 of 10 assertions.
  [r17144](https://sourceforge.net/p/sdcc/code/17144/) renamed `_spx` to `spx` in `genRet` and in
  the macro `SYM_BP`, and the library defines `_spx`. `genRet` uses the name when it finds that
  the function does not have a frame pointer.
- More faults of the called function were read from the source. `genRet` computes the frame
  pointer condition and the offset of the hidden pointer from `currFunc->stack`, which is the size
  of the frame on the internal stack. Its offset is 1 too high for the external stack, whose
  pointer has the address of the first free byte. `genFunction` adds 3 to
  `_G.stack.param_offset` for the hidden pointer only without `--xstack`. The two `AOP_DPTR`
  branches of `genRet` read the hidden pointer from internal RAM with `mov`. The change of five
  lines under Verification is for the first three of these and for `spx` in `genRet`. With it,
  `structreturn`, `bug-3849`, and `bug-4158` pass on `mcs51-xstack-auto`, and `bug-4157` fails 2
  of 12 assertions. The change was not run on the other variants.
- By the source, `genCall` emits three `dec _spx` under `--xstack` also when the result object is
  not on the stack, where `pushbigreturn` has pushed the pointer on the internal stack. This is the
  case when the calling function is not reentrant.
- `r = ((struct s (*) (void)) 0x1234) ();` ends the compiler with SIGSEGV, with each of the eight
  sets of options and with and without the patch. gdb shows a call of `genMove_o` from `genCall`
  with a null pointer as the source. By the source, `genCall` computes `bigreturn` from the pointer
  type of the literal and does not take the function type from it as `genPcall` does.
- On `mcs51-xstack-auto` with r17192 and the earlier patches of this report, the compiler stops
  for `structparam` with "code generator internal error" in `src/mcs51/gen.c`.
- Bug #3847 concerns functions that return the struct value of a call. This defect was found with
  its test cases.
